claims.text: Rendering a page involves computing styles (matching CSS to elements), layout (sizes and positions), and paint (filling pixels).
claims.source_hint: MDN: Populating the page: how browsers work (style, layout, paint)

claims.text: The browser re-renders when DOM or CSS changes affect what is visible, at rendering opportunities between tasks, and redoes only the affected steps.
claims.source_hint: HTML spec event loop 'update the rendering'; MDN: how browsers work (reflow/repaint)

claims.text: Changing an element's color triggers a repaint without layout; changing its font size changes its size and can trigger layout of elements after it, followed by paint.
claims.source_hint: MDN: how browsers work (reflow vs repaint); Chrome DevTools paint flashing

claims.text: The Đơn Hàng app (DonHang.App) is built with Flutter.

www/index.html has no CSS or script of its own, so nothing on it changes by itself after its first render; it renders again only when something outside the page's code (window resize, text selection, DevTools edits) changes what is visible.
In Chrome/Edge DevTools, the Rendering panel (⋮ → More tools → Rendering) has a Paint flashing option that highlights repainted areas in green.
claims.source_hint: Chrome DevTools docs: Rendering tab, Paint flashing

claims.text: Resizing the window causes the browser to render again.
claims.source_hint: MDN: how browsers work (reflow on viewport change)

claims.text: DOM changes made task after task (timer ticks, mouse moves) make the browser render again and again; changes inside one synchronous task render once, after the task.
claims.source_hint: reviewer r1 headless Chrome traces (256 changes/1 s → 62 layouts; 1000 changes in one loop → 1 layout)

claims.text: In Chrome/Edge DevTools, the Styles pane of the Elements panel shows an element.style block at the top for the selected element, where inline declarations can be typed.
